title: Constraint-driven theming and component variants for cost optimizer views
text:
Constraint-driven theming and component variants for cost optimizer views

description:
Create a constraint-driven theming layer and a small set of component variants focused on cost-optimizer views (cost-by-route, spend forecast, and rollout cost deltas). Deliver a Figma library with tokens, responsive grid guidance, and usage guidelines so engineering can implement predictable theming behavior across Dedicated and Hosted dashboards.

acceptance_criteria:
A Figma library file with a tokens page, three component families (metric cards, sparkline rows, rollout rail) and a usage specimen for each.
Tokens are annotated with intent (semantic token name + constraints) and token-to-kernel mappings for frontend engineers.
A short spec (2-3 pages) describing how components respond to density, result set size, and time-range filters.
Accessibility checks: color contrast >= 4.5:1 for small text, keyboard focus states documented, and aria patterns suggested for rollouts.
Two example screens (cost-dashboard and rollout-detail) implemented in the design file that can be handed off to engineering with clear tokens and CSS vars.
Design review sign-off from PM (Jonah Kim) and engineering lead (Priya Desai).

progress_updates:
2026-03-01: Kickoff — aligned scope with PM and ENG, agreed to target three component families and a tokens-first approach.
2026-03-03: Explorations — generated 6 theming constraints (density, emphasis, color mode, numeric scale, annotation density, interactive affordance). Shared initial sketches in Figma.
2026-03-06: Mid-week sync — ENG requested explicit mapping for token usage in existing cost chart codepaths; added mapping notes and lightweight CSS variable scheme.
2026-03-08: Accessibility audit pass — adjusted low-contrast label colors and added focus ring tokens. Noted remaining questions about small-viewport numeric density.
2026-03-10: Internal design review — consolidated feedback and prepared a handoff checklist; pushed design file to review mode.
2026-03-10: Waiting on PM/ENG sign-off for rollout-rail interaction pattern and final token names before merging into the Figma library.

decisions:
Adopt constraint-first tokens: each semantic token includes a short constraint (e.g., 'metric-primary: high-contrast | numeric-emphasis') so engineers can select at runtime by intent.
Reduce component variants to three density states (compact, default, spacious) instead of many granular sizes to keep engineering complexity low.
Favor explicit semantic tokens over raw color tokens in components to allow automatic theme swaps for Private deployments with stricter palettes.
Rollout rail will use a separate interaction layer (hover preview + compact inline diff) rather than inline heavy visualizations to keep dashboard performance predictable.

tradeoffs:
Smaller number of density states simplifies implementation but may require compromises for very dense enterprise screens.
Adding semantic constraints increases mental model for designers but creates stronger contract for engineering to implement dynamic theming.
Keeping rollout-rail lightweight reduces engineering cost and risk but defers more advanced inline visual diffs to a later phase.

reviewer_feedback:
Jonah Kim (PM) — +1 on tokens-first approach; requested a sample migration plan for one existing dashboard route to estimate ENG effort.
Priya Desai (ENG) — Suggested explicit CSS var names and a fallback strategy for legacy styles; asked for a small integration spike before finalizing token names.
Accessibility reviewer (Samira Ahmed) — Approved color choices after contrast updates; requested additive guidance for screen-reader order on metric cards.

next_steps:
Address ENG spike: allocate 1 week for integration spike (ENG-4821) to try tokens as CSS vars in cost-chart component.
PM to approve migration plan and schedule a cross-functional rollout window.
Merge finalized token naming into the shared Figma library and publish release notes for frontend teams.
Create a short demo recording showing density switching and rollout-rail interactions for the on-call SRE and support docs.
